title: fabric-desktop/1 — the owner channel: profiles, grants, requests, proofs and frames

mode.description: What a profile says about one row of the policy matrix. What a mode means in a row is the frozen cell (data/policy-matrix.json) and is decided by the broker's rule theory.

policy_row.description: The rows of the policy matrix (plan section 7, ADR-108 D2).

profile_rows.description: One mode per row. Two rows are fixed in every profile, custom ones included: deleting an event always asks, and deleting a calendar or changing sharing is always blocked.

profile_careful.description: The built-in profile Careful. Its name and its rows are frozen.

profile_flexible.description: The built-in profile Flexible. Its name and its rows are frozen.

profile_custom.description: A named custom profile. Each save makes a new immutable version.

custom_profile_draft.description: What the owner saves. A null id creates a profile; an id saves a new version of that one.

expansion.description: The rows a save makes more permissive, each with the mode before and after. This object is the subject of the expansion digest.

profiles.description: The profile settings: the built-in profiles, the custom ones, and the one in force.

recipient_set_source.description: Where a recipient set comes from: curated in Fabric, or imported from Google People (CD-Q06).

recipient_set_definition.description: A named selector: exact addresses, and domains matched by exact equality. A selector is not a grant.

recipient_rule.description: Who an approval covers: exact addresses, or the members of named recipient sets. There is no rule that covers everyone, so an address outside every approved recipient set always asks (G0-STRANGERS).

scope.description: What an approval or a grant covers: the calendars, each named with its account, and, where they apply, a date window and the fields for reads, the recipients for invitations, and who is notified for changes. A member that does not apply to the tools is null; a member that applies and is null covers nothing.

duration.description: How long an approval lasts. Every grant kind offers exactly these three (CD-M-DUR).

grant_term.description: A grant's duration and what it is bound to.

oneOf.description: This request only: one immutable action, used once.
This session: ends with the agent's session, the app, the broker run, or the idle timeout in the limits.
Until revoked: it has no expiry, and the null says so.

origin.description: The approval that created the grant.

policy.description: The profile version in force when the grant was created.

destination.description: Where data approved for this agent goes (R14, G0-RISK).

agent.description: An enrolled agent, shown by its registered name.

agent_drafts.description: True for the calendar the owner created in Google and selected as Agent Drafts (CD-Q05f).

account.description: A connected Google account. It never carries a token.

preferences_settings.description: The advanced calendar preferences, for every agent and profile. They ship empty: a null or an empty list means not configured (CD-Q11i).

warning_calendars.description: The calendars whose events contribute to warnings.

ruling.description: What a live proof decided against permitting an action: the failing rule, a sentence, and the proof to open. A denial carries all three so the interface can keep them on screen (DEF-7).

lifecycle_status.description: Where a request is in its lifecycle, and what that state always carries. A blocked request cannot be written without its failing rule and its proof (DEF-7).

oneOf.description: Waiting for the owner. The card expires at `approval_expires_at`.

request.description: One logical request, without private event details.

approval_card.description: What the owner is asked to approve: the scope, the duration the broker proposes, why the current authority is insufficient, and when the card expires.

approval.description: The exact snapshot of the owner's decision.

authorization.description: The broker's exact-action authorization, profile fabric-broker-authorization/1. It names the live proof that permitted the action, lives 60 seconds and is used once.

proof_report.description: The record of one live Isabelle check. It holds digests and verdicts, never calendar content.

attempt.description: One dispatch to the provider. Each has its own fresh proof.

warning.description: An advisory notice for the owner. It never blocks and never reaches an agent (G0-WARNDISC).

request_details.description: Everything the owner may open about one request. `private` holds the event content and is null when the retrieval was redacted.

before.description: The event as it was when the request was written, for a change to an existing event.

snapshot.description: The broker's state at one cursor. `requests` holds the open requests and `grants` the grants that have not ended.

change.description: One ordered change to the broker's state.

oneOf.description: The subscriber fell behind. Take a fresh snapshot and subscribe again.

params_connect_google.description: Begins the browser consent flow. A null id adds an account; an id reconnects that account.

oneOf.description: Saves a custom profile. If the save widens authority, `acknowledged_expansion` must be the digest of the expansion the owner was shown; otherwise the broker answers expansion_not_acknowledged with the expansion.
Saves a recipient set. A null id with expected revision 0 creates one.
Deletes the selector. Nothing changes at Google.

params_decide_request.description: The owner's decision on one request. `request_digest` is the digest of the request as the owner saw it. A null `selected` approves the scope as asked; a scope narrows it.

params_pause_agent.description: Pauses or resumes one agent, or all of them. Resuming does not revive a revoked grant or a session grant of an earlier run.

params_subscribe.description: Asks for every change after `cursor`, in order.

params_disconnect_google.description: Stops future dispatch for the account and ends its grants. `revoke_provider_token` also revokes Fabric's token at Google.

owner_request.description: A frame from the Tauri host to the broker. For a command the frame id is the command id.

owner_response.description: The broker's answer to an owner frame: the same id and method, and either a result or an error.

owner_notice.description: A change the broker pushes to a subscriber. Sequences rise by one; a gap means a fresh snapshot is needed.
